title: Routes by hand: static, default, discard and a virtual router
summary: Steer traffic on the Lab router with static, default and discard routes, check the result by preference and longest match, and keep a second routing table in a virtual router.

stages.title: Prefer a static route
stages.goal: Make the Lab router reach the Remote network 198.51.100.0/24 by a route you set by hand toward the Provider, so that it wins over the route OSPF already provides. The OSPF route must stay in the table as a backup. Lessons 18.2, 18.3, 18.4, 19.1.

stages.title: Add a default route
stages.goal: Give the Lab router a default route toward the Provider, so that it and the LAN host reach 10.200.0.1, an address the Provider holds but does not advertise. Lessons 18.1, 19.2.

stages.title: Drop one part of the Remote network
stages.goal: Silently discard traffic for 198.51.100.64/26 on the Lab router with a more specific route, while the rest of 198.51.100.0/24 still reaches the Provider. Lessons 3.1, 4.4, 4.5, 18.5.

stages.title: Keep a second table
stages.goal: Create a virtual router named vr1 that holds 10.255.0.1/32 on lo0.1 in a routing table of its own. That table must know nothing of the Remote network, and the main table inet.0 must not hold 10.255.0.1/32. Lesson 19.5.
